successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: 'present-day Norfolk and parts of Cambridgeshire, Lincolnshire, and Suffolk' (Lincolnshire not drawn)

ledger.x: c. 10 BC: the Iceni begin minting coins. 'The Iceni began minting coins around 10 BC'; one gold stater is captioned '15 BC - 20 AD'. The date is the start of the coinage, not of a state; Caesar does not mention the Iceni in 55 and 54 BC (they 'may be related to the Cenimagni'). [Fix pass 2026-10-19: the Iceni page…
43: the Iceni are a client kingdom of Rome.
60: Prasutagus dies and Rome treats the kingdom as its own.
after the revolt: the Iceni are 'increasingly incorporated into the Roman province'.

wars.name: Iceni revolt of 47
wars.outcome: 'In 47 the Iceni rebelled after the governor' Ostorius Scapula ordered British client kingdoms to disarm; the Iceni 'were defeated but kept their independence'.

wars.name: Boudican revolt
wars.outcome: Roman victory: Camulodunum, Londinium and Verulamium were burned in 60; the final battle's site is unknown; the Iceni were 'increasingly incorporated into the Roman province'.
